blocks.x: The project is designed to create a dataset representing people from a broad range of racial and ethnic backgrounds and physical appearances. We are seeking participation from individuals across many different communities and backgrounds.

Participants are welcome to wear religious or cultural attire and accessories in their photos, including but not limited to hijabs, turbans, kippahs, and religious jewelry. These are fully accepted, and there is no need to remove them. We want the dataset to reflect how people actually present themselves.
Participants of all racial and ethnic backgrounds are welcome to apply.

Your tasks: Design realistic, multi-step procurement and vendor management tasks with objective criteria for grading the output

micro1 is engaging experienced procurement and vendor management practitioners to design the tasks that measure what AI systems can actually do. Your domain knowledge is what matters here — no prior AI experience required.

The work is to turn real procurement workflows into benchmark tasks: realistic, difficult, and gradable against objective criteria. If you’ve built a supplier scorecard, run a weighted bid evaluation, or written a vendor risk framework, that’s exactly the instinct this needs.

i: Design multi-step tasks drawn from real procurement work — supplier assessment, bid comparison, vendor risk analysis, contract review — with realistic reference files and clear instructions.
Define objective grading criteria so two qualified reviewers would reach the same verdict on the same output.
Build tasks that require judgment rather than lookup: ones where the right answer depends on reading the materials correctly.
Create or source the supporting materials each task needs: RFP responses, pricing schedules, contracts, SLAs, risk assessments.
Flag tasks that turn out to be ambiguous or ungradable instead of submitting them anyway.
Deliver approved tasks on schedule and at the required quality level.
5+ years of hands-on responsibility in procurement, sourcing, supplier assessment, or vendor management — direct ownership of the work, not supervisory-only or adjacent exposure.
Experience creating or applying structured evaluation standards: supplier scorecards, weighted bid criteria, vendor risk frameworks, or category strategies.
Comfortable working across contracts, spreadsheets, and reports at the same time.
CIPS, CPSM or equivalent certification is a plus, but not required.
Strong English, written and spoken — B2 minimum, C1 preferred.
AI or LLM evaluation experience is a plus, but not required.
